problem.name_latex: Zeta functions of curves over finite fields
problem.statement_latex: Given a smooth projective geometrically irreducible genus-$g$ curve $C/\mathbb F_q$ in the polynomial-size representation of Kedlaya, output $P(T)\in\mathbb Z[T]$ satisfying $Z(C,T)=P(T)/((1-T)(1-qT))$. Its coefficients determine point counts over all finite extensions.
problem.statement_text: Given a smooth projective geometrically irreducible genus-$g$ curve $C/\mathbb F_q$ in the polynomial-size representation of Kedlaya, output $P(T)\in\mathbb Z[T]$ satisfying $Z(C,T)=P(T)/((1-T)(1-qT))$. Its coefficients determine point counts over all finite extensions.

quantum.headline_latex: $\operatorname{poly}(g,\log q)$ time by Kedlaya, using class-group order computations and reconstruction from cyclic resultants.
quantum.headline_text: $\operatorname{poly}(g,\log q)$ time by Kedlaya, using class-group order computations and reconstruction from cyclic resultants.

classical.headline_latex: Schoof--Pila algorithms take $(\log q)^{O_g(1)}$ time for fixed genus, with exponential dependence on genus in general. In small characteristic, $p$-adic cohomology algorithms have polynomial dependence on genus and field-extension degree, with a separate dependence on $p$ for $q=p^a$.
